Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Evergreen's Security team has a few follow-up requests as part of our procurement RFI. We need concrete attestations and evidence for two items before we can progress the purchase order:

1) Tenant-level air-gap / logical isolation model: a diagram and short narrative explaining how customer workloads are isolated at the network and process level (control plane vs data plane boundaries, sidecar vs in-host models, materially relevant encryption zones).

2) Egress and exfiltration assurances: a table showing what external endpoints (if any) Redwood services may reach from a customer tenant, per environment (hosted, dedicated, private). If any third-party telemetry or marketplace connectors are used, we need package names and optionality.

Can you provide a proof-of-concept packet (diagram + assertions + sample logs) that we can share with our audit team? If there's an NDA or additional paperwork needed to share logs, let us know.

Neha / Priyom —

Drafting notes for the packet: please review and flag any missing detail. I captured the key differences across modes and an attack-scenario summary:

1) Hosted (default):
- Control plane (managed) lives in Redwoods' control VPCs; customer data plane runs on multi-tenant worker pools with per-tenant network namespaces and per-request service tokens.
- Logical isolation: process-level namespace isolation + mandatory per-tenant KV cache segmentation.
- Egress: outbound allowed only to whitelisted service endpoints; optional marketplace connectors (S3, Slack) are disabled by default and can be enabled by tenant-admin.
- Threat note: an adversary with control-plane credentials could attempt configuration drift; mitigations include RBAC separation, signed rollout manifests, and rollback policies.

2) Dedicated:
- Dedicated GPU pools provisioned into a tenant-specific VPC — single-tenant network boundary.
- Egress controls stricter: customers can provide an allowlist; default outbound is restricted to software updates and telemetry endpoints (configurable).
- Threat note: physical resource co-residency is removed, reducing cross-tenant memory-snooping attack surface.

3) Private (VPC/On-prem):
- Control plane can be deployed as a private control-plane with customer-managed networking and optional air-gapped operation.
- Egress: fully controlled by customer's network policies; Redwood only ships agents that do not initiate outbound traffic unless explicitly configured.
- Threat note: operator error in configuration is the primary residual risk; we provide runbooks and pre-flight checks.

Artifacts I'm attaching: redwood-tenant-airgap-diagram-v1.vsdx, egress-assertion-table-20280904.csv, control-evidence-packet-evg.pdf

Priyom — please confirm CSV contains: endpoint, purpose, environment, default_state (enabled/disabled), optionality, notes.

On Thu, 6 Sep 2028 at 17:05, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai wrote:
> Alice —
>
> Quick answers inline: KMS keys are customer-scoped by default (per-tenant CMKs when requested under Dedicated/Private; hosted uses envelope keys backed by tenant-scoped DEKs encrypted with tenant-derived CMKs). Control-plane operators do not have plaintext access to tenant CMKs; we use HSM-backed KMS with requester-pays audit.
>
> On the VPC endpoint policy question: for hosted, we expose an egress gateway we control; we can enforce tenant-level allowlists. However if a tenant explicitly enables a marketplace connector, that action is audited and can be constrained via tenant allowlist settings (we can apply a blocking policy at onboarding). For enterprise customers, we typically recommend Dedicated or Private if you require absolute enforcement beyond tenant-admin controls.

> Neha

Subject: Addendum: KMS scoping and outbound policy enforcement

Alice —

Addendum (short):

- KMS scoping: Redwood supports tenant-scoped encryption keys. For Hosted customers we provide envelope encryption where each tenant gets a DEK (data encryption key) that is encrypted with a tenant-scoped CMK stored in an HSM-backed KMS. Control-plane operators cannot retrieve plaintext DEKs/CMKs. For Dedicated and Private customers we offer the option to bring-your-own-key (BYOK) or to configure a per-tenant CMK in your cloud KMS; Redwood never stores plaintext keys for BYOK setups. Audit trails capture KMS requests with requester identity and purpose.

- Outbound/VPC endpoint enforcement (hosted): The hosted runtime routes outbound connector traffic through a managed egress gateway. For enterprise tenants we support tenant-level endpoint allowlists that block connectors even if enabled by a tenant-admin; such policies are applied via RBAC and policy-engine rules and are visible in the Console. If you require network-level enforcement under your control, Dedicated (tenant VPC) or Private (customer-managed control plane) are the recommended deployment modes.

I'll attach the addendum to the packet and drop a calendar invite for a 30-minute auditor walkthrough for Friday 11:00am PT.
